clue.text: Unattractive appearance of unpleasant customer, perhaps?

definitions.text: Unattractive appearance of unpleasant customer, perhaps?

parts.words: Unattractive appearance of unpleasant customer, perhaps?
parts.note: an unpleasant person is called an ugly customer, so the quality such a person shows is a plain lack of good looks

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how a disagreeable shopper looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the state of being unsightly, the property an 'ugly customer' would have.

clue.text: Enchantment initially generating the love of Paris

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: l'amour is French for 'the love', French being Paris's language

explanation.surface: A romantic spell begins to create Parisian passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the Trojan prince; it stands for France and its language.
explanation.definitionFit: An alluring, magical charm, the original sense of the word being a spell.

clue.text: Not willing to be member of trial crew, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the answer is pronounced like the phrase described

parts.note: to be in a test eight, a rowing crew of eight on trial

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to join the jury or test team.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is a crew; one in a test eight is 'in test eight', which spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying without having made a will is to die legally will-less, which 'not willing' puns on.

clue.text: Limit attention, but cause to be loved

parts.note: end means limit or boundary
ear means attention, as in 'give ear'

explanation.surface: Restricting how much notice someone gets can make them dear.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone dear or well liked by others; win their affection.

clue.text: Job reserved across sea, producing TV entertainment

parts.note: a situation is a job or post

indicators.note: across means the reserved word stretches round the sea

parts.note: coy means shy, reserved
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A post kept for someone overseas results in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' signals one piece spanning another; 'Job reserved' reads as a post set aside, but the words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a kind of television series built on comic situations.

clue.text: First-class traveller returning aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard places the turned traveller inside the vessel

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a kind of vessel

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for traveller is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: A top-notch salesman comes home on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the traveller backwards and 'aboard' puts him in the vessel; 'traveller' as a salesman is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words of high praise meaning excellent, of the best quality.

clue.text: Fish for captain and sailorman

parts.note: skip, short for skipper, is a captain
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Seafood is being bought for a ship's master and a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipjack is a species of tuna, so an example of a sea creature with fins.

clue.text: Top man, on paper, provided rocks for building work

parts.note: an editor (ED) is the boss at a newspaper
if means provided, on condition that
ice is 'rocks' in a drink served on the rocks

explanation.surface: The editor, if paid, supplied stones for construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' means with ice, so 'rocks' is ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, imposing structure is a product of construction, a building.

clue.text: Beauty carrying a gun? It's of little significance

indicators.note: carrying means the beauty holds the other pieces inside her

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A lovely woman with a weapon turns out to be trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' signals the beauty holding the rest; 'gat' is old American slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle, a thing of no importance, is the sense here.

clue.text: Broken, as locks may be

definitions.meaning: hair (locks) is divided along a line on the head

explanation.surface: Something smashed, like a forced lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like door fastenings; here they are hair, combed to either side of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two is what something broken is, and hair combed either side of a line is said to be so.

clue.text: Rational article about family

indicators.note: about means the article goes round the family word

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
kin means family

explanation.surface: A sensible piece of writing on the subject of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece or 'a/the'; it is simply an object, and 'about' wraps it round the family word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoning being is described as a thinking one: capable of rational thought.

clue.text: Wasn't terribly constricted in this country?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the snake

parts.note: suggests the snake that squeezes its prey, the boa constrictor

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone recalls not feeling too hemmed in while visiting this nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles WASNT to TSWAN, which goes 'in' BOA, the snake 'constricted' brings to mind. Botswana is in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is an independent nation of southern Africa, an example of the defined category.

clue.text: American lawyer's fair when defending state

indicators.note: defending means the fair word surrounds and protects the state

parts.note: just means fair
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A US attorney is judged even-handed when standing up for the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link. 'when defending' wraps the fair word round the state, as a defender surrounds what it guards.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a jurist is simply an attorney, not only a legal scholar.

clue.text: Mostly suave and elegant, like an oppidan

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: urbane means suave and polished in manner

explanation.surface: A town dweller is described as fairly polished and stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: An oppidan is a town-dweller (also a pupil at Eton who boards in the town). 'Mostly' cuts the final E from URBANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppidans are townspeople, so to be like one is to belong to the city or town.

clue.text: Inattentive eccentric in huge den

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scatterbrained and odd lives in a huge lair.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking no notice or not paying heed means being careless, unobservant.

clue.text: Intermittent sound of quiet supper, for instance

indicators.note: sound of says the answer is pronounced like a phrase made from the following words

parts.note: peace is quiet, and supper is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone describes the occasional noises of a calm evening dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Done bit by bit at intervals, in fits and starts, rather than all at once.

clue.text: Parade disturbed chaps in trade centre

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A procession unsettled men at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' jumbles the chaps, and 'in' puts them inside the market; 'trade centre' is a market, not a business hub.
explanation.definitionFit: A military procession in which troops file by a saluting point is a march-by, a display.

clue.text: Boss used to control engine speed

definitions.meaning: the head, chief or person in charge
a device on an engine that regulates its speed

explanation.surface: A manager is the one regulating how fast a motor runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief or head of an institution, and also a mechanical regulator on an engine.

clue.text: Rigid camouflaged shelter beside spring

indicators.note: beside places the second piece next to the first

parts.note: a hide is a concealed shelter for watching birds or game
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: A stiff disguised hut stands next to a water source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a water source but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stuck in their ways and inflexible in outlook is narrow-minded and set, i.e. unbending.

clue.text: Old-fashioned fuel's strangely cheerless

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters of the pieces before it are jumbled

parts.note: old-fashioned means old, dated
the possessive 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Antique fuel is oddly gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' gives OLD, and 'strangely' reworks OLD with FUEL; the surface reads it as describing antique fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad and mournful, gloomy in mood.

clue.text: Animal from river in Scottish island

indicators.note: in places the river letter inside the island's name

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

explanation.surface: A creature emerges from a stream on a Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast, a creature as opposed to a human, is another word for an animal.

clue.text: Fell -— internal organ showed signs of injury

parts.note: tum is short for tummy, the stomach
bled means lost blood from a wound

explanation.surface: Someone toppled, and their gut showed damage.
explanation.definitionFit: To tumble is to fall down, so the past tense means dropped or collapsed.

clue.text: More than one description of serous membrane heard

indicators.note: heard says the answer is pronounced like the word described

parts.note: the pleura is the serous membrane round the lungs; its adjective describes it

explanation.surface: A doctor's account of a body membrane is listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical term for a form denoting several of something.

clue.text: Bind end of pole with clean material

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word that follows
material, as stuff to be shaped, signals that the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tie the tip of a stick with a fresh piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like cloth (lace, even) but signals rearranging 'clean', placed after the last letter of 'pole' ('end of').
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap round or entwine, as with laces, is to tie or fasten.

clue.text: There's a satisfactory abbreviation for this state

definitions.text: There's a satisfactory abbreviation for this state

parts.words: There's a satisfactory abbreviation for this state
parts.note: the two letters meaning all right, okay, are also the postal code of a US state

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a particular condition can be summed up as fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' reads as a condition; it is a US state whose abbreviation means 'all right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is a US state, abbreviated OK, which also means satisfactory.

clue.text: Break during march

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a march is a border region, and a fringe is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone takes a rest in the middle of a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' looks like a walk or the month; it is a frontier (as in the Welsh Marches).
explanation.definitionFit: To breach or violate a rule or right is to break it.

clue.text: Without doubt they're all yellow, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone insists that every one of them is definitely cowardly or golden.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of emphasis meaning truly, certainly, as an affirming word.

clue.text: One who forewarns others, so to speak, when driving

definitions.text: One who forewarns others, so to speak, when driving

parts.words: One who forewarns others, so to speak, when driving
parts.note: a player striking off the tee shouts 'Fore!' to alert people ahead, so is said to fore-warn

explanation.surface: A motorist who gives other road users advance warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' suggests a car; it is hitting a long shot from the tee, when the cry 'Fore!' warns those ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the sport with tees and fairways drives off and calls out a warning to those in range.

clue.text: Sounds like you will get even in this festive period

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced like a phrase built from the words that follow

parts.note: you'll is you will, and tied means drew level, got even

explanation.surface: Someone promises a listener they will settle the score over the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'you'll tied' gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yule is the old name for the Christmas season, and tide means a time or season.
